rule.description: The name is obligatory and may be accompanied by one or more given names, which then form part of the name (art. 11). The name is the one on the birth record, or the one used constantly and publicly in childhood, at least up to age 16 (art. 12). It is given by whoever declares the birth, and its choice is free (art. 13); the registrar may object only if it could harm the child (art. 14). The law sets no inheritance of the father's name
rule.source: Burundi, Code des personnes et de la famille (1993), Titre II 'Du nom', arts 11-14 (http://jafbase.fr/docAfrique/Burundi/Burundi-Code-civil.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026; BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md [B4]

rule.description: Authenticité: from 1971-72 Christian (European) given names were banned and replaced by ancestral names; nom + postnom became the identity. From 24 Apr 1990 Christian names could again be used in daily life but not in registers or official documents; from 1997 they could be registered again. Adults born before about 1997 may have records without the prénom they use

rule.description: Members of one family who share a nom must each add different complementary elements (art. 57); a parent who passes on their name must add at least one element different from their own (art. 61). So relatives may share one element, never the whole name

source: Wikipedia, Rwandan names, 'Official records', citing Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada, 'Rwanda: Procedures for obtaining the National Identity Card', 14 Oct 2010

rule.description: In speech people are usually addressed by the given name; the Kinyarwanda name is used where a formal or identifying form is needed. A name reported orally may therefore be the given name alone
rule.source: Wikipedia, Rwandan names, 'Address in spoken life'

source: Wikipedia, Rwandan names, 'Address in spoken life'

rule.description: In Kinyarwanda and French publications the Kinyarwanda name comes first, often in capitals: MUGISHA Jean
rule.source: Africana Librarians Council (ALCASA), Africana Cataloging Guidelines, '4c. Name Order', via Wikipedia, Rwandan names

source: Africana Librarians Council (ALCASA), Africana Cataloging Guidelines, '4c. Name Order', via Wikipedia, Rwandan names

rule.description: Name-initial elements described as feminine. Used ONLY to keep generated names consistent with generated sex; never to infer anyone's sex (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md C12)
rule.source: Kimenyi, A. (1978), 'Aspects of Naming in Kinyarwanda', Anthropological Linguistics 20(6): 258-271 (https://www.jstor.org/stable/30027411); RESEARCH_LOG.md, 26 Oct 2026

rule.description: Name-initial elements described as masculine. Same restriction: generation only, never inference

rule.description: Chichewa and Chitumbuka spelling has one accented letter, ŵ (standardised 1973). A Malawian writer may use it; search forms fold ŵ to w, and the original is kept
rule.source: UK Government, Malawi Toponymic Factfile, 2025, 'Languages' (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/68aee2f02f1856648215588f/Malawi_Toponymic_Factfile.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026

rule.description: Written glide clusters are pronounced with a stop: rw [ɾɡw], sw [skw], tw [tkw], bw [bɡ], mw [mŋ], by [bɟ], ry [ɾɟ], py [pc], ty [tc]. Spelling follows the letters, speech does not
rule.source: Wikipedia, Kinyarwanda, phonology (Cw/Cy table), accessed 5 Nov 2026; FSI Kirundi Basic Course, pronunciation synopsis; Nassenstein, Modern Africa (RESEARCH_LOG.md, 28 Oct 2026)

source: Wikipedia, Kinyarwanda, phonology (Cw/Cy table), accessed 5 Nov 2026; FSI Kirundi Basic Course, pronunciation synopsis; Nassenstein, Modern Africa (RESEARCH_LOG.md, 28 Oct 2026)

rule.description: Vowel length and tone are not written in the official orthography; linguistic texts write long vowels doubled (aa) and tone with accents. Search forms fold both; the original form is kept (CONCEPT-IDEA.md §5.3)
rule.source: Wikibooks, Kinyarwanda/Orthography; Kinyarwanda and Kirundi Comparative Grammar (Dunwoody Press, 2007), Table 28 (https://www.matana.de/kirundi_kinyarwanda.pdf)

source: Wikibooks, Kinyarwanda/Orthography; Kinyarwanda and Kirundi Comparative Grammar (Dunwoody Press, 2007), Table 28 (https://www.matana.de/kirundi_kinyarwanda.pdf)

rule.description: After m, the letter p stands for an aspirated [h]: impamvu [imhamvu]
[r] and [l] are one sound. Spelling uses r, except l in proper nouns that already used it and unintegrated loanwords (Kigali, Kamali). A name may be written with either letter
rule.source: 'Phonological Aspects of Loanword Adaptation in Kinyarwanda', IJLRHSS 3(3) (http://www.ijlrhss.com/paper/volume-3-issue-3/3-HSS-598.pdf); Wikibooks, Kinyarwanda/Orthography

source: 'Phonological Aspects of Loanword Adaptation in Kinyarwanda', IJLRHSS 3(3) (http://www.ijlrhss.com/paper/volume-3-issue-3/3-HSS-598.pdf); Wikibooks, Kinyarwanda/Orthography

rule.note: Chichewa (Malawi) has one r/l sound and writes it by the preceding vowel. A Malawian clerk may apply this rule to a refugee's name (Nkurunziza as Nkulunziza). The rule is sourced; that clerks apply it to foreign names is a hypothesis
rule.source: Wikipedia, Chewa language, 'Notes on the consonants' (official spelling since 1973: the r/l sound is written r after i or e, otherwise l), accessed 5 Nov 2026; Lyons & Mchombo, Chichewa Grammar ('R usually follows the vowels E and I ... L follows the vowels A, O, U'); Wiktionary, Chichewa entry guidelines

source: Wikipedia, Chewa language, 'Notes on the consonants' (official spelling since 1973: the r/l sound is written r after i or e, otherwise l), accessed 5 Nov 2026; Lyons & Mchombo, Chichewa Grammar ('R usually follows the vowels E and I ... L follows the vowels A, O, U'); Wiktionary, Chichewa entry guidelines

rule.note: Chichewa never writes c alone, so a Malawian clerk may write a c-name as ch (Ciza as Chiza)
rule.source: Peace Corps Malawi, 'An Introduction to the Chichewa Language' ('The letter C always carries an H'; no Q or X) (https://files.peacecorps.gov/multimedia/audio/languagelessons/malawi/MW_Chichewa_Language_Lessons.pdf), read 5 Nov 2026

rule.description: Ministerial order on Kinyarwanda orthography, gazetted Oct 2014, with two years to comply; it met public pushback, so old and new spellings coexist in records. The letter-level changes are NOT yet documented here: no rule is applied until the order's text is read
rule.source: The New Times, 29 Oct 2014 (https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/112825/News/how-new-orthography-will-simplify-kinyarwanda) and 17 Nov 2014 (https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/113403); Niyomugabo & Uwizeyimana (2017), Language Policy 17(3): 307-318, doi:10.1007/s10993-016-9427-x
